I'd love a set of parameters with the same refresh rate as IK Sync.

it'd need to be well maintained to support modern headsets though, the last thing we want is the promise they made of even adding individual eye blinking and then not seeing even that relatively very simple addition
Im just kinda bumping this, since i just realized today how limited the sync rate is of it as well. I used to play with visems disabled until I realized how bad it looked on the other end :(

I know there is a workaround to access IK syncing for a limited number of parameters using the expression parameters and puppet wheels, but it is limited to 8 parameters at any given time and you have to have a radial menu open on each hand for it to work which is a pain.

If there were an option to simply set a parameter to IK sync (perhaps with a limited number of parameters), or possibly just have some built into the sdk based off of unified expressions as it is more robust and universal than arkit or sranpai that would be amazing.

Otherwise the common solution is to do interpolation in the animation layers based with a much slower sync rate of playable sync parameters, which is lethargically slow.

To add on top of this request, despite there being multiple systems with proprietary facial tracking system, there should be at least a bare minimum in terms of what parameters would be used per system so they can at least match/map onto those systems if they need to be added on later down the line.

details:
If VRC had internal parameters (not tied to a specific api) we could have full face tracking without flooding the custom parameter list, it could be a tickbox on the avatar descriptor.
AFK is an example of an internal parameter that can be used and animated without needing to be added to the list of parameters, this can be done for face tracking floats as well.
title: Built-In parameters for Face tracking
